questions.prompt: What is the capital city of France?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Franks” part of the France article.

questions.proof: The modern name "France" comes from the name of the Capetian Kings of France around Paris.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with France?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture France on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the France article.

questions.proof: Metropolitan France is bordered (clockwise from the North) by Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Andorra, and Spain.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of France?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the France article.

questions.proof: France's official language is French, which is also official in 29 other countries.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “During the World War II, _____ occupied France.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “occupied”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “World Wars” part of the France article.

questions.proof: The country actively took part in both the World War I and World War II, with many battles against Germany taking place on its soil.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The climate of southern France is similar to that of _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography and climate” part of the France article.

questions.proof: The climate of southern France is similar to that of Greece.
